sentences.text: Devidas Sukdeo Ghate vs Harshida Devidas Ghate on

5
December, 2024

Author: Vikram Nath
Bench: Vikram Nath
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal Nos.13945-13946 Of 2024
 [Arising From Slp(C)Nos.5824-5825 Of 2021]
 Devidas Sukdeo Ghate Appellant(S)
 Versus
Harshida
Devidas Ghate Respondent(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.

2. These appeals arise out of order(s) dated 07.03.2020 and 05.03.2021 passed in Writ Petition No.6859 of 2018 and Review Application (Civil) No.14 of 2021 respectively, awarding interim maintenance in proceeding under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (for short, the Act),
initiated by the respondent-wife.

3. This Court, while issuing notice on 05.05.2021, had directed the appellant to deposit Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with the Registry of this Court, which amount has since accrued interest thereon, if any, be released in favour of the respondent-wife without creating any equity in her favour.
4.

The serious contention raised by learned counsel for the appellant is that the appellant and respondent were never married and as such the respondent had no right to either institute the petition under Section 9 of the Act or to claim maintenance.

He has placed reliance upon a judgment dated 29.01.2024 passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhule in Regular Criminal Case No.220 of 2014 instituted upon a complaint made by the respondent under Section 498A/494 IPC, in which acquittal was recorded with a finding that there was no valid marriage between the appellant and the respondent.
Learned counsel, therefore, submits that the entire proceedings may be quashed before the Family Court.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent, submits that the parties should allow the trial to conclude in which the parties will have adequate opportunity to give evidence and establish whether the parties were validly married or not and whether the respondent is entitled or not, to decree under Section 9 of the Act and maintenance as well, as claimed.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions advanced, we are of the view that awarding interim maintenance in such a seriously contested case may not be appropriate,
rather the Family Court should proceed with the trial and decide the petition filed under Section 9 of the Act on merits and record a finding as to whether the appellant and respondent were validly married or not.
If the Family Court finds that there was a valid marriage, it may award maintenance as well.

7. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned order(s) passed by the High Court as also the order of interim maintenance passed by the Family Court and direct the Family Court to decide the petition filed under Section 9 of the Act on merits, after affording due opportunity of producing evidence and hearing to the parties, and only thereafter consider whether maintenance should be awarded or not.
8. The Family Court may make an endevour to decide the said case expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months, subject to cooperation by both the sides.
9. The appeals stand disposed of as above.
